messages:
ada: Quick sync: prototyping a console card that attributes token cost to a "query path" (route -> routed_sku -> prefetch/cache delta). Want feedback on telemetry fields + default sampling.

james: Nice. Question: do we store per-invocation tokens_in/out or only sampled aggregates? Detailed per-invocation is heavy.

ada: Plan: full fidelity for last-5m and 1m-resolution aggregates for up to 24h. Beyond that use reservoir sampling + periodic rollups. That keeps recent drilldowns accurate.

nina: UX: card shows route-level sparkline, then expand to a stacked bar showing apportioned cache savings vs direct token cost. Clicking a bar shows top query-paths with qpath_id and sample counts.

ryan: Important: router decisions must emit a lineage_ref so we can link the original route, routing_policy, and final_sku (post-fallback). Otherwise cache credits get misattributed when fallback changes the SKU.

james: Implementation idea: emit compact event with qpath_id and light fields on every request; store full lineage map separately (small document per qpath_id). Keeps events small but queryable.

ada: Exactly. Telemetry fields proposed: qpath_id, route, router_version, routing_policy, fallback_reason (nullable), tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit (bool), prefetch_matches (int). Required: qpath_id + tokens_in. Optional: rest.

sam: From product/finance: we need a reconciliable export CSV for chargeback: qpath_id, chargeable_sku, amortized_cost_usd, granular confidence. Can that be behind an admin endpoint?

ada: Yes. I'll add POST /internal/exports/qpaths with filters (time range, routes, include_apportioned boolean). The export will include a confidence band when based on sampled data.

nina: UX tweak: default view for external customers should show 'credited owner' (single owner) to avoid confusion. Internal engineers can toggle 'apportioned' for debug. Put a short help tooltip explaining tradeoffs.

ryan: Agreed on defaults. Also ask ops to surface quota usage per-route in the same panel (burst_limit, used_in_window). That helps correlate cost spikes with quota boundaries.

james: One caveat: adding qpath_id everywhere will increase event ingestion by ~8 bytes per event plus index cardinality. We'll add qpath_id as 64-bit hashed string and route it to low-cardinality index. Also, add a flag to redact qpath_id for privacy in public logs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: schema migration "qpath-lineage-v2" deployed to canary cluster 'canary-us-west' :rocket:

ada: For the simulation widget: allow sliding % traffic between SKUs (e.g., rwd-3b -> rwd-3b-quant) and show projected delta in monthly token spend and expected cache hit change. Use recent 7d sample to extrapolate.

nina: Also show uncertainty (e.g., ±X%) derived from sample variance. Users like seeing the confidence interval.

sam: Product asks that CSV include both 'apportioned_cost' and 'credited_cost' columns so billing teams can pick which to use. Include source_note column that points to the sampling method.

ada: Will add columns. Back-of-envelope: initial export will use reservoir-based estimates for >24h and exact counts for <=24h. Make that explicit in the export metadata.

james: I'll open a telemetry PR adding qpath_id emission + lineage reference table. I'll also stub ingestion shim that materializes qpath -> lineage map in a compact store. Ping me if we need to tweak the hashed id format.

ryan: Final: make sure dashboard panel has a toggle for "Show apportioned savings (internal)" default ON for internal accounts, OFF for external. And add link to RFC in the panel footer.

ada: Great. I'll draft RFC + wireframes, and file the export API spec. Thanks.

nina: 👍

james: 👍

ryan: 👍

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary 'canary-us-west' reports new schema healthy in 1m :white_check_mark:

ada: Filing RFC now: will include sample queries, export CSV schema, and simulation math. If anyone wants to object to apportioned default for internal, speak now.

sam: No objections.
